text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nineteen people including Maulana Ziaur Rehman Farooqi, the chief of Sunni Moslem organisation Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan, photographer of a local newspaper and 13 policemen were killed when a powerful bomb exploded inside the heavily gaurded sessions court building in Punjab provincial capital Lahore.
- The caretaker government has decided to increase the prices of medicines manufactured in Pakistan by five percent.
- Widespread rains have been reported from several parts of Pakistan, breaking a long dry spell.
- The Sindh provincial government has ordered the immediate release of two Senators belonging to the Mohajir National Movement on parole.

- Deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto informed the Supreme Court that she will withdraw her petition challenging the dismissal of the National Assembly if the case is delayed beyond February 3 polls.
- Jewellers expect a 20 to 25 percent increase in sales of gold and gold jewellery during and immediately after the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan which ends mid-February.

- Pakistan has been served a legal notice for damages amounting to $2 million for suspending an agreement with Adaptive Technological Inc, California for the supply of computerised Utility Price Club Cards, sources said.
- After objections from the International Monetary Fund, the government has shelved a planned textile relief package.
- A complete strike was observed in Faisalabad in protest at the killing of Sipah-i-Sahaba leader in a bomb blast in Lahore.
- The government has restored the mobile telephone service in Karachi by permitting the Instaphone cellular phone company to resume operations.
